label: a6-010-ex-contractive-sequence-fixed-point
tail:
### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, second bullet
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "so $c = 1/3$ is the smallest admissible contraction constant"
WHY IT FAILS: The claim is false when the starting value $a = 1/2$, because then the sequence is constant ($x_k = 1/2$ for all $k$), so any $c \in (0,1)$ satisfies the contractive inequality, and there is no smallest admissible constant (the set of admissible constants is $(0,1)$, which has no minimum). The statement does not exclude this degenerate case.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Qualify the claim, for example: "for non-constant sequences, $c = 1/3$ is the smallest admissible contraction constant" or "unless the sequence is constant, $c = 1/3$ is the smallest possible constant."

0 fatal, 1 nonfatal
